newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian wheat exports seen sluggish.
newsitem.headline: Indian wheat exports seen sluggish.

text.p: Indian wheat exports are expected to remain slow until the new crop arrives in February and prices become competitive, traders said on Friday.
"India would not be able to export wheat till the new season," said Mulraj Tanna, a Bombay foodgrains exporter.
India's winter wheat crop harvest begins in February.
Traders said foreign buyers were reluctant to sign contracts as Indian wheat prices were high.
"New overseas contracts are not taking place because of high prices," said Prem Garg, a Delhi foodgrains exporter.
Traders said Indian semi-hard wheat was quoted at around $185-190 per tonne f.o.b., the same as last week. World prices were ruling at $170-175, they said.
Tanna said foreign buyers complained that Indian wheat contained the Karnal Bunt fungus.
"Unless the Karnal Bunt problem is solved, exports cannot pick up," Tanna said.
Poland, Turkey and Morocco have in recent months rejected some shipments of Indian wheat after complaining that it contained the fungus.

Karnal Bunt, also called partial bunt, is a fungus that affects wheat, durum wheat and triticale, a hybrid of wheat and rye. The fungus poses no health hazard to humans, but infected plants produce less grain and of inferior quality.

Officials of the Agricultural and Proceesed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) said the government had yet to give permission for them to allocate licences to traders for the export of 1.13 million tonnes of wheat.
"It all depends on the government when they release the orders," said J.S. Raju, a senior APEDA official.
